title: Certificates
statusUnavailable: The panel could not check which sites use the certificates.

empty.title: No certificates yet
empty.text: Issue a free certificate from an ACME certificate authority such as Let's Encrypt, or upload one you already have. Sites and the panel itself can then serve HTTPS.

issue.title: Issue certificate
issue.domainsHint: Press Enter after each name. Wildcards (*.example.com) need DNS validation; IP addresses are not allowed.
issue.caNotReady: {ca} (set it up under ACME settings first)
issue.agreement: Issuing a certificate means accepting the certificate authority's subscriber agreement.
issue.description: A free certificate from an ACME certificate authority such as Let's Encrypt.
issue.nameHint: Shown in lists; leave it empty to name it after the first domain.

challenge.http01Hint: The domains must point at this server, and port 80 must be reachable from the internet.
challenge.dns01Hint: Works for wildcards and for servers that are not reachable on port 80; needs an account at your DNS provider.

upload.title: Upload certificate
upload.intro: Paste the PEM certificate chain (the certificate first, then the intermediate certificates) and its private key, or choose the files.
upload.nameHint: Shown in lists; leave it empty to name it by the upload date.
upload.certHint: PEM: the certificate first, then the intermediate certificates.
upload.keyHint: The PEM private key of the certificate.
upload.tooBig: The file is too big for a certificate or key.

steps.check: Check that the key matches the certificate and the chain is complete
steps.store: Store the certificate and key on this server

delete.title: Delete certificate {name}?
delete.consequence: The certificate for {domains} and its private key are removed from this server. Sites and the panel must not be using it.

acme.intro: Certificates are requested from an ACME certificate authority. The contact address receives expiry and account notices from the CA.
acme.customIntro: An ACME CA you run yourself, for example step-ca. The root certificate is only used to trust the CA's own HTTPS address.
acme.rootHint: PEM of the root certificate that signs the CA's HTTPS address.
acme.eabIntro: This CA needs External Account Binding: create EAB credentials in your account at the CA and enter them here.
acme.defaultHint: Used when a certificate is issued without choosing an authority.
acme.stepUp: Saving asks for your password again.
acme.kidNeeded: Enter the key ID too: the HMAC key is used only with it.

panel.title: Panel certificate
panel.currentSelfSigned: The panel serves its own self-signed certificate.
panel.openBy: Afterwards, open the panel at {domain} so the browser accepts the certificate.
panel.noRestart: No restart is needed: the panel picks up the new certificate within a few seconds.

status.panelSelfSigned: the panel uses its self-signed certificate

panelUse.title: Use {name} for the panel?
panelUse.text: The panel serves this certificate from now on; no restart is needed.
panelUse.selfSignedTitle: Use the self-signed certificate for the panel?
panelUse.selfSignedText: The panel stops serving {name} and serves its own self-signed certificate; browsers will warn about it.

drawer.autoRenewHint: The panel renews the certificate about 30 days before it expires.
drawer.noChain: No chain is stored for this certificate.
drawer.unusedText: Neither a site nor the panel uses this certificate.
drawer.deleteNote: A certificate in use cannot be deleted: change the HTTPS settings of these sites and the panel certificate first.

steps.http01: Prove control of each name over HTTP: answer the authority under /.well-known/acme-challenge/ on port 80
steps.dns01: Prove control of each name over DNS: add _acme-challenge TXT records through {account}, then remove them
steps.store: Generate a {key} key and store the certificate and key on this server
steps.renew: Renew it automatically before it expires
